findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — Advisory P2 confidence 100: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, resource -> {` invokes `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)` for every matching resource and materializes every granted ID before returning, so administrators enumerating permissions in large realms pay unbounded per-resource authorization work and result memory; the strongest rebuttal is that the store callback streams resources, but streaming does not bound the evaluation count or the accumulated `granted` set.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:221 — Advisory P3 confidence 100: `Collection<Permission> permissions = root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server);` and its scope-matching loop are duplicated in both `hasPermission` overloads and `hasGrantedPermission`, so the next permission-result handling change requires maintainers to update three places; the strongest rebuttal is that resource resolution differs between callers, but extracting evaluation and matching after resolution deletes two duplicated evaluation-and-loop blocks while preserving those lookup boundaries.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:219 — P1 confidence 75: `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` passes a null resource into policy evaluation when an existing V2 realm lacks the newly added Clients resource, producing a server error for per-client permission checks instead of denying access; fresh-realm initialization is the strongest rebuttal but does not protect existing realms because `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — P1 confidence 100: `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) {` grants client reads immediately to an administrator with an all-clients VIEW grant even when an explicit client-specific VIEW policy denies that administrator, bypassing the object-level authorization evaluation at line 82 and exposing the denied client configuration.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:148 — [P2 confidence 100] The denial test catches ForbiddenException from `ClientScopeRepresentation clientScopeRep = clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1);` before reaching `clientResource.removeDefaultClientScope(clientScopeRep.getId());`, so it passes when unauthorized scope removal is allowed and gives maintainers false confidence in the write authorization check.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — [advisory P2 confidence 100] Granting `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)` simultaneously leaves the new role-mapping scope separation unverified and lets a regression authorizing either operation with the wrong scope pass; although the combined grant proves the happy path, the preceding no-permission checks do not exercise either operation with only the other scope granted.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:99 — [advisory P2 confidence 100] The new `return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE);` branch has no corresponding client-scope-role mapping case in the changed integration tests, so maintainers receive no regression signal when that advertised scope stops granting or restricting mappings; although PermissionClientTest exercises user-role and composite mappings, those invoke different evaluator methods and never cover this branch.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
